notes: Measures how long the virtual pad takes to show each press, release, trigger pull and stick onset after the receiver reports it (kernel timestamps on both sides, per event). It is the evidence for the receiver-takeover gate (docs/plans/receiver-takeover-plan.md 9.3): G4a, Driver digital p50 is 0.5 ms or less; G4b, Driver is at least 0.2 ms lower than App on digital and on stick onset. Both passes run back to back in one session (App path, then Driver LIVE), so the two reports share the mapping and the template and can be compared with scripts/tools/dev-run-compare.py A.json B.json, which prints the per-step latency columns and a one-line gate summary. Each step also has to pass as an ordinary check (ten flicks, ten taps of A and of B, five full RT pulls). Do the movements the same way in both passes; the hands-still gate waits for you between steps. Added 2026-11-09 for T8.

steps.detail: Snap the left stick out to the rim and let go so it springs back to centre by itself, ten times, about one a second. Wait for it to settle between flicks. Leave the right stick alone.
steps.title: Flick the LEFT stick hard and let it spring back, 10 times

steps.detail: Press A and let go again, ten times, at an easy pace (a few a second). Each press and each release is timed.
steps.title: Tap A 10 times

steps.detail: Press B and let go again, ten times, at an easy pace (a few a second). Each press and each release is timed.
steps.title: Tap B 10 times

steps.detail: Squeeze RT all the way down and let it come fully back up, five times, with a short pause between.
steps.title: Pull RT all the way and release, 5 times

steps.detail: Push it to the rim and go all the way round, slowly, once or twice, then release it. Leave the right stick alone.
steps.title: Roll the LEFT stick in one or two slow circles, then let go

title: Latency: controller to pad, per press (App, then Driver) — T8 gate
